correctness.rationale: For all primes p, n≥2, 1≤s<n, the nilpotent commutative ring multiplication p^s ab on Z/p^n gives a radical brace. Its canonical λ_a(b)=(1+p^s a)b; factors form principal units U_s, and right maps preserve these same unit orbits, so indecomposable components are exactly U_s-orbits. Valuation v<k=n-s gives size p^(k-v) and (p-1)p^(s-1) orbits per size p^j; v≥k plus zero gives p^s singletons. Canonical flip iff p^s ab=0 mod p^n, so within size p^j component every pair flips exactly if 2j≤k, whereas singleton pairs always flip. Counting pairs yields Pr(F)=[p+k(p-1)]/p^(k+1), Pr(C)=[p^s+(p-1)p^(s-1)Σ_{j=1}^k p^(2j)]/p^(2n), joint with j≤floor(k/2). As k→∞ at fixed p,s, Pr(F)→0,Pr(C)→p^(1-s)/(p+1). Tested eight independent finite prime-power cases with actual action and pair enumeration; universal proof is valuation orbit/count argument.

originality.rationale: The radical-ring-to-brace construction and Ferrara–Trombetti–Tsang general four flip probabilities and orbit-square law are prior. The result adds all p,n,s orbit multiplicities, all-or-none internal threshold, evaluated joint event law and asymptotic separation. Darlington–Wiertel classify indecomposable solutions with given permutation braces rather than the canonical full-brace solution, so no direct implication is established. Ferrara full text is relevant and unavailable for direct full comparison this run; older cyclic brace classifications could implicitly include part of these formulas.
